Order 
This is the first criminal appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14(2) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for grant of bail relating to FIR No. 329 of 2024 registered at Police Station- Gwalior, District Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 366, 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC and Sections, 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(2)(v), 3(2) (va) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

sentences.text: 2. Prosecution story in brief is that present appellant - accused committed rape with the prosecutrix on many occasions on the false pretext of marriage and threatened her to face dire consequences to her as well as her daughter in case, she will inform the Police.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he is innocent and NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:15561 2 CRA-10461-2024 has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further argued the appellant has not committed any offence and did not indulge in any kind of act as alleged by the prosecutrix.

Further submission is that as per prosecution story, incident said to have taken place between 15.04.2020 to 01.12.2023, however, the FIR has been lodged by prosecutrix on 01.06.2024 with unexplained delay.
It is further argued that appellant and prosecutrix were in relationship and the appellant never assured the prosecutrix for marriage.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant is permanent resident of District Gwalior (M.P.) and there is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence.

It is further submitted that the appellant is ready and willing to co-operate in the investigation and shall abide by all the terms and conditions as may be imposed by this Court; therefore, he prays for grant of anticipatory bail.
5.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the application and argued that there is sufficient material available on record to connect the appellant with NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15561 3 CRA-10461-2024 the crime.
It is further argued that the present appellant is absconding since date of registration of FIR and is not cooperating in the investigation.
Further argument is that the investigation is in early stage and more evidence is yet to be collected, more so, custodial interrogation of the appellant is very much needed.

It is further argued that the offence punishable u/S. 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act prima-facie appears to exist and therefore statutory bar contained u/S. 18 of the Act comes in way of the appellant, hence, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
Under these circumstances, he prayed for rejection of present bail application by contending that on the basis of material available on record no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.

6. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary available on record.
7.

In this case necessary ingredients to constitute offence under SC/ST Act are disclosed on plain reading of allegations levelled against the appellant, therefore, the case law cited by appellant in the case of Shajan Skaria (supra) & Prithvi Raj Chauhan (supra), do not help the appellant as there is specific bar of Section 18 of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for grant of anticipatory bail.
8. It would not be desirable to enter into merits of the rival contentions at this juncture.
It is well settled that the considerations governing grant of anticipatory bail are altogether different from those relevant for the prayer for regular bail.

9. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:15561 4 CRA-10461-2024 but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, in the considered opinion of this Court, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
10. Consequently, instant criminal appeal is hereby dismissed.
